title: Nepal Opens Everest for First Time Since Quakes
main_content:
Nepal has opened Mount Everest to climbers for the autumn season, the first time since a deadly earthquake triggered an avalanche that killed 18 climbers earlier this year.

Japanese climber Nobukazu Kuriki will be the first person to make a solo attempt at reaching the 8,850-meter summit. It will be his fifth attempt at climbing Everest. His four previous bids were unsuccessful. His last, in 2012, ended him with losing 9 fingers to frostbite.

His climb will take place in the autumn season, which is not a popular time for trekkers due to extreme temperatures and less daylight.

During a ceremony Sunday in Katmandu, Kuriki said he wanted to give a positive message about Nepal and spread the word that the country was safe for climbers and trekkers.

More than 400 teams were forced to abandon their attempts after the earthquake-triggered avalanche destroyed a popular trekking route.

The devastating April 25 earthquake left nearly 9,000 people dead.

Nepal has since been struggling to draw tourists and trekkers back to the country. Mountaineering and tourism accounts for a significant percentage of the country’s gross domestic product.

Nepal is home to eight of the world’s 14 peaks measuring at over 8,000 meters.

questions.question: Why was Everest closed to trekkers?
options: A series of avalanches destroyed a significant number of climbing permits.
The Nepalese government wanted to prioritize safety after an earthquake.
Climbers were not able to make it to base camp due to heavy snowfall.
Health regulations prevented climbers from entering high altitudes.
questions.answer: The Nepalese government wanted to prioritize safety after an earthquake.

questions.question: How many times did Nobukazu Kuriki attempt to reach the top of Mount Everest?
options: Three previous attempts before this one.
Four previous attempts before this one.
Five previous attempts before this one.
Six previous attempts before this one.
questions.answer: Four previous attempts before this one.

questions.question: Why don’t trekkers usually climb Everest in the autumn season?
options: Due to financial difficulties faced by trekkers during this season.
Extreme temperatures and less daylight make climbing difficult.
Many climbers prefer to undertake expeditions in the spring.
Autumn season brings an increased risk of rockfalls.
questions.answer: Extreme temperatures and less daylight make climbing difficult.
